claim: Putting a character inside an in-world aperture states confinement, surveillance or distance in one move and without a line of dialogue. Doorway and fence say we are watching him from outside something; mirror says we are seeing a version of him rather than him.
method: identical subject sentence and seed in every panel; only the option clause changes. panels marked control render the untouched subject, because SDXL cannot express absence.

panels.clause: framed by a doorway, seen through a door
seen through a window, window frame in the foreground
reflection in a mirror, seen in a mirror, mirror frame
framed by leaves, foliage in the foreground, branches at the edges
framed by silhouetted heads, blurry people in the foreground
framed by curtains, curtain in the foreground
seen through a tunnel mouth, dark tunnel edges
seen through a chain-link fence, fence in the foreground

review.issue: doorway, window, mirror, foliage and curtain are objects a floodlit soccer stadium does not contain. Animagine will honour the aperture by relocating the scene, so those panels change the location as well as the framing device — the option clause ends up rewriting the subject even though it never restates it in text.
review.fix: Prefer apertures the location can supply: "seen through a chain-link fence", "seen through the tunnel mouth, dark edges", "framed by goal netting", "framed by silhouetted heads in the foreground". Drop curtain, foliage and mirror, or move this card to a scene that contains them.
